Run a read-only MCP server giving access to a chTKCat instance

Source: R/mcp.R
chTKCat_mcp_server.Rd

Start a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server communicating through the standard input and output (stdio transport). The server lets an AI assistant (e.g., Claude Code, Claude Desktop) explore and query the MDBs available in a chTKCat instance, relying on their descriptions and data models.

Usage

chTKCat_mcp_server(
  host = Sys.getenv("TKCAT_HOST", "localhost"),
  port = as.integer(Sys.getenv("TKCAT_PORT", "9111")),
  user = Sys.getenv("TKCAT_USER", "default"),
  password = Sys.getenv("TKCAT_PASSWORD", ""),
  https = as.logical(Sys.getenv("TKCAT_HTTPS", "FALSE")),
  maxRows = 1000L,
  maxChars = 60000L,
  maxExecutionTime = 300L,
  ...
)

Arguments

host

a character string specifying the host heberging the database (default: TKCAT_HOST environment variable or "localhost")

port

an integer specifying the port on which the database is listening (default: TKCAT_PORT environment variable or 9111)

user

user name (default: TKCAT_USER environment variable or "default")

password

user password (default: TKCAT_PASSWORD environment variable or "")

https

a logical indicating if the HTTPS protocol should be used (default: TKCAT_HTTPS environment variable or FALSE)

maxRows

maximum number of rows returned by a query (default: 1000)

maxChars

maximum number of characters returned by a tool call (default: 60000). Longer outputs are truncated.

maxExecutionTime

maximum execution time of a query in seconds (default: 300)

...

additional parameters for chTKCat() (only the default driver, ClickHouseHTTP::ClickHouseHTTP(), is supported).

Value

No return value, called for side effects: the function returns when the input stream is closed by the MCP client.

Details

The function is not supposed to be called in an interactive R session: it is launched by the MCP client with a command such as Rscript -e "TKCat::chTKCat_mcp_server()". See vignette("TKCat-MCP", package = "TKCat") for installation and configuration instructions.

Read-only access. The server cannot write, create or delete anything and cannot modify grants:

  • the ClickHouse session is opened with the readonly = 2 setting: the server rejects any query modifying data, tables, databases, users or grants, and the readonly setting cannot be changed afterwards;

  • SQL statements are checked before being sent: only single SELECT queries (possibly starting with WITH) are accepted, without SETTINGS nor INTO OUTFILE clauses and without table functions accessing external resources (e.g., url(), file(), s3(), remote());

  • the data accessible to the server are limited to those accessible to the ClickHouse user. Using a dedicated user with limited permissions is recommended.

Available tools.

  • list_mdbs: list the MDBs with their description and access level.

  • search_tkcat: search MDBs, tables and fields by keyword.

  • describe_mdb: general information, tables and relationships of an MDB.

  • describe_tables: detailed data model of MDB tables (fields, types, keys, indexes, collection members).

  • preview_table: first records of a table or of a matrix.

  • query_mdb: run a read-only ClickHouse SQL query on an MDB.

  • get_matrix_values: get values from a matrix table.

  • list_collections: collections and their members used to integrate MDBs.

Environment variables. The default values of the connection parameters are taken from the following environment variables: TKCAT_HOST, TKCAT_PORT, TKCAT_USER, TKCAT_PASSWORD and TKCAT_HTTPS.

See also

chTKCat_mcp_http_server(), chTKCat(), explore_MDBs()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
## From a terminal (normally launched by the MCP client)
# TKCAT_HOST=localhost TKCAT_PORT=9111 TKCAT_USER=default \
#   Rscript -e "TKCat::chTKCat_mcp_server()"
} # }
